objective: Prove, for chains of three rings joined by two shared contacts (PROCESS-CHAIN-20261108-001's setting): (1) the composing lags of a chain are eventually periodic with the period of its T-step maps, and observing the chain only at one residue of that period gives a process in which composition holds at every observed lag or at none, so intermittent composition is persistent composition of a strobed process whose phase is the only input not fixed by the chain; (2) for linear or affine chains composition at lag T holds exactly when the far contact depends on both end rings at T (arrival is composition), so the composing lags are fixed by the chain's own dynamics; (3) for any chain, composition at lag T implies that the far contact depends on both end rings at T. Check on the chains of PROCESS-CHAIN-20261108-001B.
status: Proved 2026-11-08: composing lags recur with the period of the T-step maps, so intermittent composition is persistent composition of a strobed chain whose phase is the only outside input; linear and affine chains compose exactly where the far contact depends on both end rings (arrival); in any chain composition implies arrival.
title: When intermittent composition is a law
